patient.name: Jonah Reyes
patient.background: First-year student, lives in crowded dorm, skipped meningitis booster vaccine.

initial_symptoms.text: Deep aching pain in both legs

findings.result: Tiny purple spots that don't fade when pressed (petechiae)
Low platelets, clotting factors used up (early DIC)
Cold limbs, slow capillary refill, no clot (poor perfusion)
Bones and muscles intact, no fracture (normal X-ray)
Mild neck stiffness, no abscess yet (early meningism)
Producing less urine, creatinine creeping up (pre-renal injury)
Racing heart, blood pressure starting to drop (tachycardia)

treatments.name: IV ceftriaxone plus fluids
treatments.why: A third-generation cephalosporin rapidly kills Neisseria in the blood, and fluids support failing circulation.
treatments.attending_line: Antibiotics for a bacterial infection. Revolutionary. Someone call the Nobel committee.

treatments.name: Heparin for suspected leg clot
treatments.why: No DVT exists; thinning blood when DIC has already used up clotting factors triggers bleeding.
treatments.attending_line: Great, you treated a clot that doesn't exist and made him bleed everywhere.

treatments.name: Ibuprofen and rest (flu)
treatments.why: It masks fever while bacteria multiply, and NSAIDs harm kidneys and stomach in shock.
treatments.attending_line: Sure, it's the flu. Flu famously makes non-blanching rashes. Wait, no.

treatments.name: IV acyclovir (antiviral)
treatments.why: Antivirals do nothing to bacteria, delay real treatment, and acyclovir crystals can injure dehydrated kidneys.
treatments.attending_line: Lovely antiviral. The bacteria thank you for the extra six hours.

post_mortem: Jonah caught Neisseria meningitidis from a shared vape in his crowded dorm, and it spread through his bloodstream, causing septic shock and early DIC. Leg pain, cold hands and feet, and a rash that didn't fade when pressed in an unvaccinated student should have meant IV antibiotics right away.
